subject.title: [Feature]: Fallback approval mode + model attribution in messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in approval gate before executing configured model fallbacks, and if so what config shape, timeout behavior, and channel delivery contract should it use?
rationale: The remaining request changes provider/model fallback behavior and adds config surface, and repository policy treats fallback behavior and config additions as product- and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Design a core opt-in fallback gate
options.body: Define a default-off per-agent approval contract with timeout, deny/proceed behavior, channel delivery, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep fallback automatic
options.body: Treat current fallback notices plus responsePrefix model attribution as the supported visibility/control model and close fallback approval as not planned.

options.title: Route through extension API first
options.body: Design a generic approval/event extension point for fallback decisions instead of adding a one-off core model config key.

recommendation.title: Design a core opt-in fallback gate
recommendation.body: Define a default-off per-agent approval contract with timeout, deny/proceed behavior, channel delivery, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-history signal across fallback docs, fallback behavior, and agent model config schema.
